claim: The structure of the higher plant PSI-LHCI super-complex was determined at 2.8 Å resolution.
source: Here, we report the structure of the higher plant PSI-LHCI super-complex determined at 2.8 Å resolution.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the resolution achieved for the structure determination.

claim: The PSI-LHCI super-complex structure includes 16 subunits.
source: The structure includes 16 subunits and more than 200 prosthetic groups, which are mostly light harvesting pigments.
evidence: The abstract directly states the number of subunits in the structure.

claim: The PSI-LHCI super-complex structure includes more than 200 prosthetic groups.
source: The structure includes 16 subunits and more than 200 prosthetic groups, which are mostly light harvesting pigments.
evidence: The abstract directly states the number of prosthetic groups.

claim: The four LhcA subunits of LHCI include 52 chlorophyll a molecules.
source: The complete structures of the four LhcA subunits of LHCI include 52 chlorophyll a and 9 chlorophyll b molecules, as well as 10 carotenoids and 4 lipids.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the number of chlorophyll a molecules in the four LhcA subunits.

claim: The four LhcA subunits of LHCI include 9 chlorophyll b molecules.
source: The complete structures of the four LhcA subunits of LHCI include 52 chlorophyll a and 9 chlorophyll b molecules, as well as 10 carotenoids and 4 lipids.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the number of chlorophyll b molecules in the four LhcA subunits.

claim: The four LhcA subunits of LHCI include 10 carotenoids.
source: The complete structures of the four LhcA subunits of LHCI include 52 chlorophyll a and 9 chlorophyll b molecules, as well as 10 carotenoids and 4 lipids.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the number of carotenoids in the four LhcA subunits.

claim: The four LhcA subunits of LHCI include 4 lipids.
source: The complete structures of the four LhcA subunits of LHCI include 52 chlorophyll a and 9 chlorophyll b molecules, as well as 10 carotenoids and 4 lipids.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the number of lipids in the four LhcA subunits.

claim: Oxygenic photosynthesis converts sunlight into chemical energy in plants, green algae, and cyanobacteria.
source: Oxygenic photosynthesis, in which the conversion of sunlight into chemical energy by plants, green algae, and cyanobacteria, occurs, underpins the survival of virtually all life forms.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field of photosynthesis.

claim: Oxygenic photosynthesis produces oxygen and assimilates carbon dioxide into organic matter.
source: By producing oxygen and assimilating carbon dioxide into organic matter, this process determines, to a large extent, the composition of our atmosphere and provides essential food and fuel.
evidence: This is a fundamental characteristic of oxygenic photosynthesis.

claim: PSI contains approximately 200 antenna pigments.
source: After an additional photon is absorbed by any of the 200 antenna pigments of PSI, its energy migrates through this large network of connected pigments and eventually oxidizes P700, a special chlorophyll pair located at the center of PSI.
evidence: The text explicitly states the number of antenna pigments in PSI.

claim: P700 is a special chlorophyll pair located at the center of PSI.
source: After an additional photon is absorbed by any of the 200 antenna pigments of PSI, its energy migrates through this large network of connected pigments and eventually oxidizes P700, a special chlorophyll pair located at the center of PSI.
evidence: The text explicitly describes P700 as a special chlorophyll pair at the center of PSI.

claim: Oxygenic photosynthesis evolved over 3 billion years ago in cyanobacteria.
source: Oxygenic photosynthesis evolved over 3 billion years ago in cyanobacteria (Blankenship, 1992; Barber, 2004; Nelson, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The first photosynthetic eukaryotes appeared approximately 1.5 billion years ago.
source: Later, approximately 1.5 billion years ago, the first photosynthetic eukaryotes appeared, eventually evolving into land plants roughly 0.5 billion years ago.
evidence: This is a statement about evolutionary history presented in the manuscript.

claim: Land plants evolved roughly 0.5 billion years ago.
source: Later, approximately 1.5 billion years ago, the first photosynthetic eukaryotes appeared, eventually evolving into land plants roughly 0.5 billion years ago.
evidence: This is a statement about evolutionary history presented in the manuscript.

claim: The crystal structure of plant PSI was first reported at 4.4 Å resolution.
source: The crystal structure of plant PSI was first reported at 4.4 Å resolution (Ben-Shem et al., 2003) and has been improved up to 3.3 Å resolution in the last decade (PDB 2WSC).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ben-Shem et al., 2003.

claim: The plant PSI structure has been improved up to 3.3 Å resolution in the last decade.
source: The crystal structure of plant PSI was first reported at 4.4 Å resolution (Ben-Shem et al., 2003) and has been improved up to 3.3 Å resolution in the last decade (PDB 2WSC).
evidence: This claim references a specific PDB entry (2WSC) indicating prior structural work.

claim: The previous PSI preparation was limited to pea plants from the variety Alaska.
source: This PSI preparation was limited to pea plants from the variety Alaska, and good crystals were hard to come by (Amunts et al., 2007, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Amunts et al., 2007, 2010.

claim: The new crystals belonged to space group P212121.
source: In contrast to the P21 symmetry of the previous crystal, the current crystal belonged to higher symmetry space group P212121.
evidence: This is a direct observation from crystallographic analysis.

claim: The previous crystal had P21 symmetry.
source: In contrast to the P21 symmetry of the previous crystal, the current crystal belonged to higher symmetry space group P212121.
evidence: This is a comparison with previously published crystallographic data.

claim: In the P21 crystal, the PSI-LHCI complex was organized as parallel layers in which the iron-sulfur clusters FX, FA and FB face the adjacent P700.
source: In the P21 crystal the PSI-LHCI complex was organized as parallel layers in which the iron-sulfur clusters FX, FA and FB face the adjacent P700 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A showing the crystal organization.

claim: The complexes inside the new crystal lattice were serially arranged in a criss-crossed manner in which the polarity of each PSI unit contrasts another.
source: The complexes inside the new crystal lattice were serially arranged in a crissed-crossed manner in which the polarity of each PSI unit contrasts another (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1B showing the new crystal organization.

claim: The current crystals generated no net voltage.
source: Consequently, the current crystals generated no net voltage (data not shown), whereas a voltage of up to 50 V was recorded (Toporik et al., 2012) upon illumination of dried P21 crystals placed on electron conductive material.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: A voltage of up to 50 V was recorded upon illumination of dried P21 crystals placed on electron conductive material.
source: Consequently, the current crystals generated no net voltage (data not shown), whereas a voltage of up to 50 V was recorded (Toporik et al., 2012) upon illumination of dried P21 crystals placed on electron conductive material.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Toporik et al., 2012.

claim: The entire structure was eventually re-built with more than 35,000 atoms.
source: Starting with a minimal model containing only the three natively bound iron-sulfur clusters, the entire structure was eventually re-built with more than 35,000 atoms (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, see 'Material and methods' section for details).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model building process with reference to figures.

claim: The structure of plant PSI includes 12 core subunits bound with four light-harvesting proteins comprising the LHCI antenna complex.
source: The structure of plant PSI includes 12 core subunits bound with four light-harvesting proteins comprising the LHCI antenna complex.
evidence: This is a direct description of the structural composition.

claim: The entire complex contains 214 prosthetic groups, including 156 chlorophylls (nine assigned as chlorophyll b), 32 carotenes, and 14 lipids.
source: The entire complex contains 214 prosthetic groups, including 156 chlorophylls (nine assigned as chlorophyll b), 32 carotenes, and 14 lipids, many of them located at key contact points of the complex.
evidence: This is a direct enumeration of prosthetic groups in the structure.

claim: The core photosynthetic reaction centers have remained virtually unchanged over the entire 2 billion years of their evolution.
source: The core photosynthetic reaction centers have remained virtually unchanged over the entire 2 billion years of their evolution (Jordan et al., 2001; Ben-Shem et al., 2003; Amunts et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to structural studies.

claim: The root-mean-square deviation (rmsd) between the plant and cyanobacterial core (PDB 1JB0) decreased from 1.1 Å to 0.55 Å compared to the previous model (PDB 2WSC).
source: Compared to our previous model (PDB 2WSC), the root-mean-square deviation (rmsd) between the plant and cyanobacterial core (PDB 1JB0) decreased from 1.1 Å to 0.55 Å.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison between structural models.

claim: The dramatic change from trimer to monomeric organization that occurred in eukaryotes was triggered by the addition of the PsaH subunit.
source: The dramatic change from trimer to monomeric organization that occurred in eukaryotes, was triggered by the addition of the PsaH subunit (Ben-Shem et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ben-Shem et al., 2003.

claim: PsaH binds four other core subunits.
source: A new configuration for PsaH shows that this subunit binds four other core subunits.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the current study.

claim: PsaH enters the membrane surrounding PsaL to prevent PSI trimerization and associates with PsaI and PsaB via mostly hydrophobic interactions.
source: PsaH then enters the membrane surrounding PsaL to prevent PSI trimerization and associates with PsaI and PsaB via mostly hydrophobic interactions (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by Figure 3A.

claim: Eukaryotes can modulate the distribution of excitation energy transfer between their two photosystems via a mechanism called state transitions.
source: Eukaryotes can modulate the distribution of excitation energy transfer between their two photosystems via a mechanism called state transitions (Lunde et al., 2000; Bellafiore et al., 2005; Rochaix, 2011; Rochaix et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Under state II conditions, PSI associates with a mobile pool of the LHCII antennae, which increases its absorbance cross-section.
source: Under state II conditions, PSI associates with a mobile pool of the LHCII antennae, which increases its absorbance cross-section (Kargul et al., 2005; de Bianchi et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kargul et al., 2005 and de Bianchi et al., 2010.

claim: Genetic studies suggest that PsaH, PsaL, and PsaK play important roles in state transitions.
source: Genetic studies suggest that PsaH, PsaL, and PsaK play important roles in this process (Scheller et al., 2001; Zhang and Scheller, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to genetic studies.

claim: Electron microscopy studies have identified the binding site of the additional antennae complexes along the PsaL/PsaH-PsaK side.
source: Electron microscopy studies have identified the binding site of the additional antennae complexes along the PsaL/PsaH-PsaK side (Kargul et al., 2005; Kouril et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to electron microscopy studies.

claim: A new chlorophyll bound by PsaH was identified at the current resolution.
source: A new chlorophyll bound by PsaH was identified at the current resolution.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the current study.

claim: The plant PSI complex forms a stable complex with its electron donor plastocyanin (PC), which results in a thousand-fold acceleration of the electron transfer rate.
source: One of the distinguishing characteristics of the eukaryotic PSI is the stable complex it forms with its electron donor PC, which results in a thousand-fold acceleration of the electron transfer rate (Bottin and Mathis, 1985).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bottin and Mathis, 1985.

claim: The PC binding site consists of three elements: a positive patch on PsaF, a hydrophobic patch on PsaA and PsaB, and a PsaA luminal loop.
source: Three elements make up the PC binding site: the first is a positive patch located along the helix-turn-helix N-terminal domain of PsaF (Hippler et al., 1997, 1998; Ben-Shem et al., 2003). The second element is a hydrophobic patch composed of two parallel helices in PsaA and PsaB (Figure 2B) (Sommer et al., 2006; Kuhlgert et al., 2012). The third conserved feature of the PC binding site is a PsaA luminal loop protruding from the generally flat luminal surface of PSI.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations and reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The plant PC binding site is buried deeper in the complex compared to the cyanobacterial binding site.
source: However, it is clear that the plant binding site is buried deeper in the complex, this is achieved by the extension of the PsaF N-terminal and by the new position of the N-terminus of PsaH, which forms a loop mirroring the conformation of the conserved luminal PsaA loop, suggesting a direct role for PsaH in PC binding.
evidence: This is a structural comparison between plant and cyanobacterial PSI.

claim: The PSI core is a highly efficient hub onto which diverse antennae systems connect.
source: The PSI core is a highly efficient hub onto which diverse antennae systems connect such as phycobilisomes and IsiA-like assemblies in cyanobacteria and red algae and LHC type antennae in eukaryotes (Berera et al., 2009; Engelken et al., 2010; Nelson and Junge, 2015; Wahadoszamen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The core pigment organization is conserved across kingdoms despite diversity in connected antenna.
source: Remarkably, the core pigment organization is conserved across kingdoms despite this diversity in connected antenna (Amunts et al., 2007; Busch and Hippler, 2011; Croce and van Amerongen, 2013), which suggests that the connection points between the core and the antennae are conserved.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations and includes an inference about connection points.

claim: The existence of red-absorbing pigments (or 'red traps') is a general property of PSI.
source: The existence of red-absorbing pigments (or 'red traps') is a general property of PSI (Morosinotto et al., 2005; Wientjes et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Morosinotto et al., 2005 and Wientjes et al., 2012.

claim: Most of the eukaryotic red pigments have been shown to reside at LHCI.
source: Most of the eukaryotic red pigments have been shown to reside at LHCI.
evidence: This is a statement about the location of red pigments in eukaryotic PSI.

claim: A stacked chlorophyll trimer supported by an extended loop in PsaB was the best candidate for one of the strong red absorbers in thermophilic cyanobacteria PSI.
source: A stacked chlorophyll trimer supported by an extended loop in PsaB was the best candidate for one of the strong red absorbers in this complex (Jordan et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jordan et al., 2001.

claim: PsaB sequences from eukaryotes and many cyanobacteria lack the extended loop that supports the chlorophyll trimer in thermophilic cyanobacteria.
source: PsaB sequences from eukaryotes and many cyanobacteria lack this extended loop, resulting in this chlorophyll trimer being lost, as has been shown in the plant and mesophilic PSI structures (Amunts et al., 2010; Mazor et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Amunts et al., 2010 and Mazor et al., 2014.

claim: A new core chlorophyll was observed bound between PsaG and Lhca1 and a newly discovered lipid.
source: At the current resolution, we observed new core chlorophyll bound between PsaG and Lhca1 and a newly discovered lipid (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the current study supported by Figure 4A.

claim: The new chlorophyll restores the stacked chlorophyll trimer independent of the shortened PsaB loop.
source: This new chlorophyll restores the stacked chlorophyll trimer independent of the shortened PsaB loop and is responsible for one of the connection points between the core complex and the LHCI antenna, with a Mg–Mg distance of 12.5 Å between it and chlorophyll 1010 in Lhca1 (the nomenclature for LHCII is used to describe Lhcas [Standfuss et al., 2005]).
evidence: This is a structural observation with a specific distance measurement.

claim: Chlorophyll trimers located at the periphery of the core antenna are extremely important for antenna attachment and are probably general attachment points to the core.
source: We suggest that chlorophyll trimers located at the periphery of the core antenna are extremely important for antenna attachment and are probably general attachment points to the core that are utilized not only by eukaryotes, but also by other antenna systems in cyanobacteria.
evidence: This is a suggestion based on structural observations.

claim: Only six pigment pairs connect LHCI to the core antenna in the current structure.
source: In contrast to the previous plant structures, which included a small pool of 'Gap chlorophylls', only six pigment pairs connect LHCI to the core antenna in the current structure.
evidence: This is a structural observation comparing the current structure to previous ones.

claim: Lhca1 is the main connector for excitation transfer, harboring three chlorophylls that are within 14 Å of reaction center pigments.
source: Lhca1 is the main connector for excitation transfer, harboring three chlorophylls that are within 14 Å of reaction center pigments (Figure 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by figures showing distances.

claim: Lhca3 is one of the main connection points with two chlorophyll pairs connecting to the core.
source: Surprisingly, Lhca3 is also one of the main connection points with two such pairs (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by Figure 4C.

claim: The extremely fast and efficient energy transfer processes in PSI-LHCI occur through only six pairs of pigment molecules located at three sites.
source: To summarize, the extremely fast and efficient energy transfer processes that typify PSI-LHCI occurs through only six pairs of pigment molecules located at three sites.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on structural observations.

claim: The LHCI belt is located on the PsaF side of the PSI core.
source: The LHCI belt is located on the PsaF side of the PSI core.
evidence: This is a structural observation about the location of LHCI.

claim: On the stromal face of the membrane, the four conserved N-terminal domains connect each Lhca subunit to its neighbor through interaction with an Lhca-specific loop (loop 23).
source: On the stromal face of the membrane, the four conserved N-terminal domains connect each Lhca subunit to its neighbor through interaction with an Lhca-specific loop (loop 23) (Figure 5A) that follows immediately after the second transmembrane helix and supports a new chlorophyll site (numbered 16) in Lhca4 and Lhca2 (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by figures.

claim: Lhca1 completely lacks loop 23 and instead contains a short, positively charged linker in this region.
source: Lhca1, which interacts with PsaG in the core complex, completely lacks this loop and instead contains a short, positively charged linker in this region (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by Figure 5A.

claim: One of the major changes in the structure of LHCI is the reversal in the polarity of PsaG.
source: One of the major changes in the structure of LHCI is the reversal in the polarity of PsaG.
evidence: This is a structural observation comparing the current structure to previous ones.

claim: Genetic analysis in plants has revealed that each Lhca subunit has a specific binding site.
source: Genetic analysis in plants has revealed that each subunit has a specific binding site and, with the exception of the Lhca4-Lhca5 pair, the various Lhcas are not interchangeable (Lucinski et al., 2006; Wientjes et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to genetic studies.

claim: With the exception of the Lhca4-Lhca5 pair, the various Lhcas are not interchangeable.
source: Genetic analysis in plants has revealed that each subunit has a specific binding site and, with the exception of the Lhca4-Lhca5 pair, the various Lhcas are not interchangeable (Lucinski et al., 2006; Wientjes et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to genetic studies.

claim: All four Lhcas are remarkably similar to each other and to LHCII.
source: All four Lhcas are remarkably similar to each other and to LHCII.
evidence: This is a structural comparison observation.

claim: The extended loop 23 supports a new chlorophyll-binding site (numbered 16), common to Lhca4 and Lhca2.
source: The extended loop 23 supports a new chlorophyll-binding site (numbered 16), common to Lhca4 and Lhca2 (Figure 6A,B) and an additional chlorophyll site, coordinated by transmembrane helix two, connects the two partners of each heterodimer.
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by figures.

claim: Nine chlorophyll b sites were assigned in LHCI based on electron density maps.
source: We were able to assign nine chlorophyll b sites in LHCI based on electron density maps (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a structural observation based on electron density maps.

claim: Four binding sites for chlorophyll b were detected in the high resolution structure of LHCII.
source: Four binding sites for chlorophyll b were detected in the high resolution structure of LHCII (Liu et al., 2004; Standfuss et al., 2005) as well as in the structure of CP29 (Pan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published structures.

claim: The distribution of chlorophyll b sites in LHCI is markedly uneven, with three sites located in Lhca2, two sites found at Lhca1, three sites at Lhca4 and a single site on Lhca3.
source: The distribution of chlorophyll b sites in LHCI is markedly uneven, with three sites located in Lhca2 (2010, 2011 and 2013), two sites found at Lhca1 (site 1009 and 1010), three sites at Lhca4 (4010, 4011 and 4013) and a single site on Lhca3 (site 3011).
evidence: This is a structural observation about chlorophyll b distribution.

claim: These findings are consistent with mutational data which identified more chlorophyll b sites on Lhca2 than on Lhca3.
source: These findings are consistent with mutational data which identified more chlorophyll b sites on Lhca2 then on Lhca3 (Castelletti et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to mutational data.

claim: Lhca1 and Lhca3 are the main junctions for excitation energy transfer from LHCI to the PSI core.
source: The high number of chlorophyll b pigments in Lhca2 and the fact that its closest connection to the core is mediated by chlorophyll b (site 2010, shown in Figure 4D) is consistent with our suggestion that Lhca1 and Lhca3 are the main junctions for excitation energy transfer from LHCI to the PSI core.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations.

claim: The structures of Lhca3 and Lhca4 clearly show a coordinating asparagine residue unique to the red chlorophyll site.
source: The structures of Lhca3 and Lhca4 clearly show a coordinating asparagine residue unique to this site (Arnoux et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by a citation.

claim: The red pigments of Lhca3 and Lhca4 are tilted approximately 12° relative to their orientation in LHCII, Lhca1, and Lhca2.
source: The configurations of the pigments themselves differed, with the red pigments of Lhca3 and Lhca4 tilted approximately 12° relative to their orientation in LHCII, Lhca1, and Lhca2 due to a second change from a bulky leucine residue at position 64 of LHCII to glycine and alanine in Lhca3 and Lhca4, respectively (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is a structural observation with specific angle measurements.

claim: Three luteins at position L3 bridge the chlorophylls at site 6 in Lhca1, Lhca3, and Lhca4 to PsaG, Lhca2, and Lhca1.
source: Additional connections that stabilize LHCI are formed by three luteins at position L3. These luteins bridge the chlorophylls at site 6 in Lhca1, Lhca3, and Lhca4 to PsaG, Lhca2, and Lhca1 (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by figures.

claim: NPQ was recently reported in PSI.
source: First discovered in the PSII complex, NPQ was recently reported in PSI.
evidence: This is a statement about recent findings in the field.

claim: NPQ sites are located on LHC proteins bound by the hydroxylated carotenoid zeaxanthin, which quenches harmful chlorophyll triplets.
source: NPQ sites are located on LHC proteins bound by the hydroxylated carotenoid zeaxanthin, which quenches harmful chlorophyll triplets (Standfuss et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Standfuss et al., 2005.

claim: A new chlorophyll site (numbered 17) coordinated by a histidine residue is located at the heterodimer interface of both Lhca1/4 and Lhca2/3.
source: A new chlorophyll site (numbered 17) coordinated by a histidine residue (histidine 150 in Lhca4 and histidine 170 in lhca3) is located at the heterodimer interface of both Lhca1/4 and Lhca2/3.
evidence: This is a structural observation about a new chlorophyll site.

claim: In the Lhca1/4 interface, a new carotenoid site (numbered 4505 or L5) forms co-planar π systems with the ring of chlorophyll 4017.
source: In the Lhca1/4 interface, a new carotenoid site (numbered 4505 or L5) forms co-planar π systems (plane to plane distance 3.7 Å) with the ring of chlorophyll 4017, positioning it in a configuration that should provide efficient photo-protection from chlorophyll triplets (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is a structural observation with specific distance measurements.

claim: The carotenoid site L5 is proposed to be the site of NPQ in LHCI.
source: We propose that this is also the site of NPQ in LHCI, and this fits well with the experimental observation (Standfuss et al., 2005) that the zeaxanthin responsible for NPQ is located near the red pair in the PSI-LHCI luminal gap region.
evidence: This is a proposal based on structural observations and cited experimental data.

claim: Zeaxanthin is synthesized from violaxanthin by violaxanthin deepoxidase (VDE) as part of the xanthophyll cycle in response to lumen acidification.
source: In response to lumen acidification, zeaxanthin is synthesized from violaxanthin by violaxanthin deepoxidase (VDE) as part of the xanthophyll cycle.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the xanthophyll cycle.

claim: Both the activity and location of VDE are regulated by pH changes.
source: Both the activity and location of VDE are regulated by pH changes (Ballottari et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ballottari et al., 2014.

claim: At low pH, VDE is activated and binds the luminal side of the membrane, gaining access to its substrate.
source: At low pH, VDE is activated and binds the luminal side of the membrane, gaining access to its substrate.
evidence: This is a statement about VDE regulation.

claim: On the luminal side, a large gap (25 Å) separates LHCI from the core.
source: On the luminal side, a large gap (25 Å) separates LHCI from the core.
evidence: This is a structural observation with a specific distance measurement.

claim: The luminal side of PSI-LHCI contains patches of negative potential distributed on both sides of the PSI-LHCI gap.
source: The complete modeling of LHCI side chains shows that the luminal side of PSI-LHCI contains patches of negative potential distributed on both sides of the PSI-LHCI gap (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a structural observation based on electrostatic calculations shown in Figure 7.

claim: The negative charge characteristic of the luminal side of PSI-LHCI is an important feature regulating the accessibility of VDE to the PSI-LHCI gap.
source: We suggest that the negative charge characteristic of the luminal side of PSI-LHCI is an important feature regulating the accessibility of VDE to the PSI-LHCI gap.
evidence: This is a suggestion based on structural observations.

claim: Under low light conditions, the relatively high luminal pH will result in strong repulsive forces between negative patches and the acidic domain of VDE, preventing VDE from binding to PSI.
source: Under low light conditions, the relatively high luminal pH will result in strong repulsive forces between these negative patches and the acidic domain of VDE, preventing VDE from binding to PSI.
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal based on electrostatic considerations.

claim: Under high light, acidification of lumen will result in partial neutralization of negative patches and allow VDE access to the PSI-LHCI gap regions.
source: Under high light, acidification of lumen, which is known to trigger VDE activity, will result in partial neutralization of these patches and allow VDE access to the PSI-LHCI gap regions (Arnoux et al., 2009) (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal supported by a citation and Figure 7D.

claim: Carotene L4505 is ideally positioned to be exchanged easily via the VDE accessibility mechanism.
source: Carotene L4505 is ideally positioned to be exchanged easily via this mechanism (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural positioning shown in Figure 7C.

claim: In the current structure, position L5 is occupied with zeaxanthin.
source: In the current structure, position L5 is occupied with zeaxanthin; however, the pigment assignment cannot be definite, even at the current resolution.
evidence: This is a structural observation with a caveat about assignment certainty.

claim: Pea seeds (Pisum sativum var. Kalvadon) were used for PSI purification.
source: Pea seeds (Pisum sativum var. Kalvadon) were washed with running water for 6–8 hr and seeded in a vermiculite tray.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the plant material used.

claim: The new crystals could be obtained from several pea plant varieties.
source: Therefore, we screened for new robust crystals that are abundant, stable, and much more uniform. The new crystals could be obtained from several pea plants varieties, a large proportion of them diffracted to 3 Å with several yielding higher resolutions.
evidence: This is a methodological observation about crystal quality.

claim: A large proportion of the new crystals diffracted to 3 Å with several yielding higher resolutions.
source: The new crystals could be obtained from several pea plants varieties, a large proportion of them diffracted to 3 Å with several yielding higher resolutions.
evidence: This is a methodological observation about crystal diffraction quality.
